verses.1: Then the LORD addressed Job out of the storm and said:
verses.2: Who is this that obscures divine plans with words of ignorance?
verses.3: Gird up your loins now, like a man; I will question you, and you tell me the answers!
verses.4: Where were you when I founded the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding.
verses.5: Who determined its size; do you know? Who stretched out the measuring line for it?
verses.6: Into what were its pedestals sunk, and who laid the cornerstone,
verses.7: While the morning stars sang in chorus and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
verses.8: And who shut within doors the sea, when it burst forth from the womb;
verses.9: When I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its swaddling bands?
verses.10: When I set limits for it and fastened the bar of its door,
verses.11: And said: Thus far shall you come but no farther, and here shall your proud waves be stilled!
verses.12: Have you ever in your lifetime commanded the morning and shown the dawn its place
verses.13: For taking hold of the ends of the earth, till the wicked are shaken from its surface?
verses.14: The earth is changed as is clay by the seal, and dyed as though it were a garment;
verses.15: But from the wicked the light is withheld, and the arm of pride is shattered.
verses.16: Have you entered into the sources of the sea, or walked about in the depths of the abyss?
verses.17: Have the gates of death been shown to you, or have you seen the gates of darkness?
verses.18: Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know all:
verses.19: Which is the way to the dwelling place of light, and where is the abode of darkness,
verses.20: That you may take them to their boundaries and set them on their homeward paths?
verses.21: You know, because you were born before them, and the number of your years is great!
verses.22: Have you entered the storehouse of the snow, and seen the treasury of the hail
verses.23: Which I have reserved for times of stress, for the days of war and of battle?
verses.24: Which way to the parting of the winds, whence the east wind spreads over the earth?
verses.25: Who has laid out a channel for the downpour and for the thunderstorm a path
verses.26: To bring rain to no man's land, the unpeopled wilderness;
verses.27: To enrich the waste and desolate ground till the desert blooms with verdure?
verses.28: Has the rain a father; or who has begotten the drops of dew?
verses.29: Out of whose womb comes the ice, and who gives the hoarfrost its birth in the skies,
verses.30: When the waters lie covered as though with stone that holds captive the surface of the deep?
verses.31: Have you fitted a curb to the Pleiades, or loosened the bonds of Orion?
verses.32: Can you bring forth the Mazzaroth in their season, or guide the Bear with its train?
verses.33: Do you know the ordinances of the heavens; can you put into effect their plan on the earth?
verses.34: Can you raise your voice among the clouds, or veil yourself in the waters of the storm?
verses.35: Can you send forth the lightnings on their way, or will they say to you, "Here we are"?
verses.36: Who puts wisdom in the heart, and gives the cock its understanding?
verses.37: Who counts the clouds in his wisdom? Or who tilts the water jars of heaven
verses.38: So that the dust of earth is fused into a mass and its clods made solid?
verses.39: Do you hunt the prey for the lioness or appease the hunger of her cubs,
verses.40: While they crouch in their dens, or lie in wait in the thicket?
verses.41: Who provides nourishment for the ravens when their young ones cry out to God, and they rove abroad without food?

notes.text: Now the LORD enters the debate and addresses two discourses (Job 38-39 and Job 40-41) to Job, in which he speaks of his wisdom and power, which are altogether beyond the capacity of Job, who therefore should never dare to demand a reason for the divine actions. Out of the storm: frequently the background of the appearances of the LORD in the Old Testament; cf Psalm 18; 50; Nahum 1:3; Hebrews 3.
Gird up your loins: prepare for combat - figuratively, be ready to defend yourself in debate.
Hail... of war: thus God used a hailstorm to rout Joshua's foes in the battle of Gibeon; cf Joshua 10:11; Sirach 46:5.
Pleiades... Orion... Bear: cf Job 9:9. Mazzaroth: It is uncertain what astronomical group is meant by this Hebrew word; perhaps a southern constellation (cf Job 9:9).
Veil yourself... storm: wrap yourself in a cloud, as God comes in a theophany; cf Psalm 18:12.
Here we are: at your service.
Understanding: the reflection of divine Wisdom discernible in the created animal instincts of the cock.
